*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: generate_outputs.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+DATA = ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet"
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_motorist_killed)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths,
+           SUM(number_of_cyclist_killed)::BIGINT AS cyclist_deaths,
+           COUNT(*) AS crash_rows,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL) AS motorist_null_rows,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_cyclist_killed IS NULL) AS cyclist_null_rows,
+           MIN(crash_date) AS first_date,
+           MAX(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [str(DATA)],
+).df()
+
+requested = annual[annual["year"].between(2013, 2025)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
+assert requested["year"].tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert (requested["motorist_null_rows"] == 0).all()
+assert (requested["cyclist_null_rows"] == 0).all()
+assert (requested["first_date"].astype(str) == requested["year"].astype(str) + "-01-01").all()
+assert (requested["last_date"].astype(str) == requested["year"].astype(str) + "-12-31").all()
+
+values = requested[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths"]].copy()
+values.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+
+years = values["year"].to_numpy()
+motorists = values["motorist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+cyclists = values["cyclist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+width = 0.38
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6.5))
+ax.bar(years - width / 2, motorists, width, label="Motorists", color="#345995")
+ax.bar(years + width / 2, cyclists, width, label="Cyclists", color="#e07a5f")
+ax.set_title("NYC traffic deaths by road-user group, 2013–2025")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths")
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+ratios = values.copy()
+ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"] = ratios["motorist_deaths"] / ratios["cyclist_deaths"]
+ratios.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6.5))
+ax.plot(years, ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"], color="#345995", marker="o", linewidth=2.2)
+ax.axhline(1, color="#666666", linewidth=1, linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
+ax.set_title("Motorist deaths relative to cyclist deaths, NYC 2013–2025")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_ylabel("Motorist deaths per cyclist death (ratio)")
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+out_of_range = annual[~annual["year"].between(2013, 2025)]
+out_of_range_exclusion = "; ".join(
+    f"{int(row.year)}: 100% of its {int(row.crash_rows):,} rows excluded (outside the requested interval)"
+    for row in out_of_range.itertuples(index=False)
+)
+omission_text = (
+    "Within 2013–2025, 0% of rows are omitted for NULL motorist or cyclist death counts in every year, "
+    "and no included year is partial (each year has dates from January 1 through December 31). "
+    f"The year filter excludes {out_of_range_exclusion}."
+)
+
+ratio_series = ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"]
+max_idx = ratio_series.idxmax()
+min_idx = ratio_series.idxmin()
+max_year = int(ratios.loc[max_idx, "year"])
+min_year = int(ratios.loc[min_idx, "year"])
+max_ratio = float(ratio_series.loc[max_idx])
+min_ratio = float(ratio_series.loc[min_idx])
+gap = values["motorist_deaths"] - values["cyclist_deaths"]
+max_gap_idx = gap.idxmax()
+min_gap_idx = gap.idxmin()
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual deaths in each road-user group",
+            "denominator": "None (absolute death counts)",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist)",
+            "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart",
+            "reason": "Absolute counts directly show the number of motorist and cyclist deaths in each year.",
+            "probability": 0.65,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; the count gap ranged from "
+                f"{int(gap[min_gap_idx])} in {int(values.loc[min_gap_idx, 'year'])} to "
+                f"{int(gap[max_gap_idx])} in {int(values.loc[max_gap_idx, 'year'])}, and 2025 had "
+                f"{int(values.iloc[-1]['motorist_deaths'])} motorist deaths versus "
+                f"{int(values.iloc[-1]['cyclist_deaths'])} cyclist deaths."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how many motorist and cyclist deaths occurred in each requested year; "
+                "the bars show more motorist deaths in every year, with the smallest absolute gap in "
+                f"{int(values.loc[min_gap_idx, 'year'])} and largest in {int(values.loc[max_gap_idx, 'year'])}. "
+                "Annual counts are a defensible direct comparison of the two death totals, but they do not measure "
+                "death risk per traveler or per trip because exposure denominators are not in this file. "
+                + omission_text
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual ratio of motorist deaths to cyclist deaths",
+            "denominator": "Cyclist deaths in the same calendar year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "The ratio makes the relative scale of motorist and cyclist death counts comparable across years.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths were {min_ratio:.1f} times cyclist deaths in {min_year} (the lowest ratio) "
+                f"and {max_ratio:.1f} times in {max_year} (the highest); the 2025 ratio was "
+                f"{float(ratio_series.iloc[-1]):.1f}."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the relative number of motorist deaths compared with cyclist deaths "
+                f"changed year by year: the ratio ranged from {min_ratio:.1f} in {min_year} to "
+                f"{max_ratio:.1f} in {max_year}, and was {float(ratio_series.iloc[-1]):.1f} in 2025. "
+                "A same-year ratio is a defensible way to compare relative counts when the groups have different "
+                "totals, but it does not show the absolute size of the death counts or death risk per traveler. "
+                + omission_text
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+with (OUT / "options.json").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+    json.dump(options, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+    f.write("\n")
+
+print(values.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"ratio range: {min_ratio:.6f} ({min_year}) to {max_ratio:.6f} ({max_year})")
+print(omission_text)
*** End Patch

@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+DATA = ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet"
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_motorist_killed)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths,
+           SUM(number_of_cyclist_killed)::BIGINT AS cyclist_deaths,
+           COUNT(*) AS crash_rows,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL) AS motorist_null_rows,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_cyclist_killed IS NULL) AS cyclist_null_rows,
+           MIN(crash_date) AS first_date,
+           MAX(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [str(DATA)],
+).df()
+
+requested = annual[annual["year"].between(2013, 2025)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
+assert requested["year"].tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert (requested["motorist_null_rows"] == 0).all()
+assert (requested["cyclist_null_rows"] == 0).all()
+assert (requested["first_date"].astype(str) == requested["year"].astype(str) + "-01-01").all()
+assert (requested["last_date"].astype(str) == requested["year"].astype(str) + "-12-31").all()
+
+values = requested[["year", "motorist_deaths", "cyclist_deaths"]].copy()
+values.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+
+years = values["year"].to_numpy()
+motorists = values["motorist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+cyclists = values["cyclist_deaths"].to_numpy()
+width = 0.38
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6.5))
+ax.bar(years - width / 2, motorists, width, label="Motorists", color="#345995")
+ax.bar(years + width / 2, cyclists, width, label="Cyclists", color="#e07a5f")
+ax.set_title("NYC traffic deaths by road-user group, 2013–2025")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_ylabel("Deaths")
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+ax.legend(frameon=False)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+ratios = values.copy()
+ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"] = ratios["motorist_deaths"] / ratios["cyclist_deaths"]
+ratios.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6.5))
+ax.plot(years, ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"], color="#345995", marker="o", linewidth=2.2)
+ax.axhline(1, color="#666666", linewidth=1, linestyle="--", alpha=0.7)
+ax.set_title("Motorist deaths relative to cyclist deaths, NYC 2013–2025")
+ax.set_xlabel("Year")
+ax.set_ylabel("Motorist deaths per cyclist death (ratio)")
+ax.set_xticks(years)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+out_of_range = annual[~annual["year"].between(2013, 2025)]
+out_of_range_exclusion = "; ".join(
+    f"{int(row.year)}: 100% of its {int(row.crash_rows):,} rows excluded (outside the requested interval)"
+    for row in out_of_range.itertuples(index=False)
+)
+omission_text = (
+    "Within 2013–2025, 0% of rows are omitted for NULL motorist or cyclist death counts in every year, "
+    "and no included year is partial (each year has dates from January 1 through December 31). "
+    f"The year filter excludes {out_of_range_exclusion}."
+)
+
+ratio_series = ratios["motorist_to_cyclist_ratio"]
+max_idx = ratio_series.idxmax()
+min_idx = ratio_series.idxmin()
+max_year = int(ratios.loc[max_idx, "year"])
+min_year = int(ratios.loc[min_idx, "year"])
+max_ratio = float(ratio_series.loc[max_idx])
+min_ratio = float(ratio_series.loc[min_idx])
+gap = values["motorist_deaths"] - values["cyclist_deaths"]
+max_gap_idx = gap.idxmax()
+min_gap_idx = gap.idxmin()
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual deaths in each road-user group",
+            "denominator": "None (absolute death counts)",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist)",
+            "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart",
+            "reason": "Absolute counts directly show the number of motorist and cyclist deaths in each year.",
+            "probability": 0.65,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; the count gap ranged from "
+                f"{int(gap[min_gap_idx])} in {int(values.loc[min_gap_idx, 'year'])} to "
+                f"{int(gap[max_gap_idx])} in {int(values.loc[max_gap_idx, 'year'])}, and 2025 had "
+                f"{int(values.iloc[-1]['motorist_deaths'])} motorist deaths versus "
+                f"{int(values.iloc[-1]['cyclist_deaths'])} cyclist deaths."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how many motorist and cyclist deaths occurred in each requested year; "
+                "the bars show more motorist deaths in every year, with the smallest absolute gap in "
+                f"{int(values.loc[min_gap_idx, 'year'])} and largest in {int(values.loc[max_gap_idx, 'year'])}. "
+                "Annual counts are a defensible direct comparison of the two death totals, but they do not measure "
+                "death risk per traveler or per trip because exposure denominators are not in this file. "
+                + omission_text
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual ratio of motorist deaths to cyclist deaths",
+            "denominator": "Cyclist deaths in the same calendar year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "The ratio makes the relative scale of motorist and cyclist death counts comparable across years.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": (
+                f"Motorist deaths were {min_ratio:.1f} times cyclist deaths in {min_year} (the lowest ratio) "
+                f"and {max_ratio:.1f} times in {max_year} (the highest); the 2025 ratio was "
+                f"{float(ratio_series.iloc[-1]):.1f}."
+            ),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how the relative number of motorist deaths compared with cyclist deaths "
+                f"changed year by year: the ratio ranged from {min_ratio:.1f} in {min_year} to "
+                f"{max_ratio:.1f} in {max_year}, and was {float(ratio_series.iloc[-1]):.1f} in 2025. "
+                "A same-year ratio is a defensible way to compare relative counts when the groups have different "
+                "totals, but it does not show the absolute size of the death counts or death risk per traveler. "
+                + omission_text
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+with (OUT / "options.json").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+    json.dump(options, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+    f.write("\n")
+
+print(values.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"ratio range: {min_ratio:.6f} ({min_year}) to {max_ratio:.6f} ({max_year})")
+print(omission_text)
